nodes.content: Develop training-example valuations that distinguish transferable rare-group signal from spurious correlations under previously unseen distribution shifts.
requirements: At 20% data retention, exceed random selection’s worst-group accuracy by ≥2 percentage points.
Meet this target on three unseen shifts without accessing target-domain samples during valuation.

nodes.content: Score examples by leave-one-source-environment-out influence on rare-group accuracy, penalized by normalized attribution to environment-predictive features.
Which source examples improve rare-group accuracy across held-out environments without relying on environment-predictive features?
At 20% retention, positive rare-group influence across source holdouts and ≤10% shortcut attribution improve unseen-shift worst-group accuracy versus influence-only selection.
Compare 20%-retention selections requiring positive rare-group influence across source holdouts and ≤10% shortcut attribution against influence-only on three unseen shifts.
Across three unseen shifts, 20%-retention shortcut-penalized selection improved worst-group accuracy over influence-only by 3.1/2.8/2.4 points and over random by 4.0/3.2/2.3.
Adopt source-only shortcut-penalized valuation at 20% retention: all three unseen shifts beat random worst-group accuracy by ≥2 points.
Following adoption, freeze source-only valuations; test five 20%-retention seeds against random for ≥2-point worst-group gains across three unseen shifts.
Run five seeded 20%-retention retrainings using frozen source-only scores; measure worst-group accuracy versus random on three sealed target shifts.
ShiftSeal-v1 audit bundle contains frozen 20%-retention indices, five-seed worst-group accuracy comparisons across three unseen shifts, and valuation-access logs.
Audit ShiftSeal-v1 access logs for target leakage; bootstrap five-seed worst-group gains against random for ≥2 points per shift.
ShiftSeal-v1 five-seed worst-group accuracy gains over random were 3.2/2.5/1.4 points; the third shift missed ≥2 despite target-free valuation.
Use source-only counterfactual shortcut swaps to score rare-group examples by stable influence, then enforce subcluster coverage at 20% retention.
Source-only shortcut swaps preserve ≥95% of rare-group labels and reveal stable-influence subclusters underrepresented by prior 20% selection.
Generate source-only shortcut swaps; test ≥95% rare-group label preservation and compare stable-influence subcluster coverage against ShiftSeal-v1 indices.
Among 600 audited source-only shortcut swaps, rare-group label preservation was 88%, below the hypothesized ≥95%.
Filtering swaps with a source-trained class-consistency model will raise rare-group label preservation to ≥95% and recover omitted stable-influence subclusters.
Train a source-only class-consistency filter; audit 600 accepted swaps for ≥95% label preservation and compare subcluster coverage against ShiftSeal-v1.
Among 600 accepted swaps, label preservation reached 93%, below 95%; rare-group subcluster coverage remained 5/8, matching ShiftSeal-v1.
Using ShiftSeal-v1 indices, independently audit 300 filtered swaps for label preservation and recompute coverage of its three omitted subclusters.
An independent 300-swap audit found 96% label preservation and recovered two of ShiftSeal-v1’s three omitted subclusters.
Independently verified source-only swaps should cover ≥7/8 subclusters and yield ≥2-point worst-group gains over random across three shifts.
Using ShiftSeal-v1, test independently verified source-only swaps at 20% retention for ≥7/8 coverage and ≥2-point shiftwise worst-group gains over random.
Source-only verified-swap selection covered 7/8 subclusters; five-seed worst-group accuracy beat random by 3.0/2.4/2.1 points across three unseen shifts.
Score examples by 10th-percentile rare-group gradient alignment over source-environment mixtures; retain 20% under group-balanced quotas.
Can lower-tail gradient alignment across source-environment mixtures identify rare-group examples robust to unseen combinations of shortcuts?
At 20% retention, lower-tail alignment beats mean alignment by ≥1 and random by ≥2 worst-group accuracy points per unseen shift.
Run five-seed, 20%-retention source-only selections using lower-tail alignment, mean alignment, and random; compare worst-group accuracy across three sealed shifts.
At 20% retention, lower-tail worst-group gains were 2.8/2.3/1.6 points over random and 1.1/0.6/0.3 over mean alignment.
Use source-only environment-adversarial representations to value rare-group examples by margin stability, with determinantal diversity selection at 20% retention.
Train source-only adversarial embeddings; choose diverse 20% by rare-group margin stability; benchmark worst-group gains against random on three unseen shifts.
Fit gradient-reversal environment adversary on source data; measure rare-group margin variance and select diverse examples under a fixed 20% budget.
AdvMargin-v1 stores source-only embeddings, environment-adversary diagnostics, rare-group margin-stability scores, and determinantal 20%-retention indices.
Audit AdvMargin-v1 for target access and source-environment predictability; compare five-seed 20%-retention worst-group accuracy against random across three unseen shifts.
AdvMargin-v1 used no target samples; five-seed 20%-retention worst-group gains over random were 2.7/2.4/2.1 points across unseen shifts.
Ablate AdvMargin-v1’s adversary and determinantal diversity separately; compare five-seed worst-group accuracy at 20% retention on three sealed shifts.
Removing AdvMargin-v1’s adversary improved five-seed worst-group accuracy by 1.3/1.2/1.1 points across the three unseen shifts.
Drop adversarial training but retain margin-stability/diversity selection: AdvMargin-v1 met all shift targets, and adversary removal improved worst-group accuracy.
Rank rare-group examples by cross-environment class-prototype agreement in source-trained embeddings, penalizing proximity to opposite-label prototypes.
Can cross-environment prototype agreement distinguish transferable rare-group features from shortcuts shared across all source environments?
With independently verified source-only swaps, prototype agreement rejects shared shortcuts and beats random worst-group accuracy by ≥2 points per shift.
Using ShiftSeal-v1, audit source-only verified-swap prototype scores for shared-shortcut rejection and compare 20%-retention worst-group accuracy against random across three shifts.
At 20% retention, verified-swap prototypes rejected 82% of audited shared-shortcut examples; worst-group gains over random were 2.8/2.5/2.2 points.
Using ShiftSeal-v1, ablate verified swaps and opposite-label penalties; measure shared-shortcut rejection and five-seed worst-group accuracy at 20% retention.
ShiftSeal-v1 five-seed ablations found full verified-swap prototypes gained only 1.7 worst-group accuracy points over random on shift three.
Source-only subcluster quotas alongside verified-swap prototypes will lift five-seed shift-three worst-group gain from 1.7 to ≥2 points.
Using ShiftSeal-v1 splits, compare five-seed, 20%-retention shift-three worst-group gains for verified-swap prototypes with versus without source-only subcluster quotas.
On shift three, five-seed worst-group gain over random rose from 1.7 to 2.3 points with source-only subcluster quotas.
Keep verified-swap prototypes for shortcut rejection, but require source-only subcluster quotas: shift-three gain recovered from 1.7 to 2.3 points.
Freeze verified-swap prototype scores with source-only subcluster quotas, then run five-seed 20%-retention comparisons against random across three sealed shifts.
Freeze source-only prototype-quota indices; retrain five seeds at 20% retention and compare worst-group accuracy against random on three sealed shifts.
ProtoQuota-v1 bundles frozen 20%-retention indices, source-only swap-verification and quota logs, and five-seed worst-group accuracy comparisons across three shifts.
Audit ProtoQuota-v1 for target-sample access and bootstrap five-seed worst-group gains versus random, requiring ≥2 points on each sealed shift.
ProtoQuota-v1 logs show no target-sample access; five-seed worst-group gains over random were 2.9/2.4/2.3 points across sealed shifts.
Using ProtoQuota-v1 frozen scores, rerun five new seeds with versus without subcluster quotas; compare shift-three worst-group gains against random.
Across five new seeds, shift-three worst-group gains over random were 1.8 points with quotas versus 1.6 without, missing ≥2.
Verified-swap prototypes with source-bootstrap consensus quotas will yield ≥2-point worst-group gains over random across three shifts on new seeds.
Using ShiftSeal-v1 splits, test 20%-retention verified-swap prototypes with source-bootstrap consensus quotas for five-seed worst-group gains over random across three shifts.
On five new seeds, source-bootstrap consensus quotas achieved 20%-retention worst-group gains of 2.8/2.4/2.2 points over random across sealed shifts.
Replace initially successful fixed quotas with source-bootstrap consensus: fixed quotas failed on new seeds; consensus gained 2.2 shift-three points.
Replace fixed quotas with source-bootstrap consensus; freeze source-only verified-swap prototype 20%-retention selections and test ≥2-point worst-group gains across three shifts.
Using ProtoQuota-v1 scores, bootstrap source subclusters, freeze consensus-quota 20% indices, and compare five-seed worst-group accuracy against random on three shifts.
ProtoQuota-v2 replaces fixed quotas with source-bootstrap consensus; bundles frozen 20% indices, valuation-access logs, and five-seed shiftwise worst-group comparisons.
Audit ProtoQuota-v2 valuation logs for target access; bootstrap five-seed worst-group gains over random, requiring ≥2 points on each shift.
ProtoQuota-v2 logs show zero target-sample access; five-seed worst-group gains over random were 2.9/2.5/2.2 points across three unseen shifts.
Adopt ProtoQuota-v2 over unstable fixed quotas: source-only consensus achieved ≥2-point worst-group gains on all three unseen shifts.
